headline.technical: US stocks rose (S&P 500 1.60%, Nasdaq Composite 2.31%) as investors bought battered AI shares (Mint), but CNBC reported the S&P 500 is in a November correction.
headline.layman: US stocks bounced on Friday as investors bought AI shares that had fallen, but CNBC says the S&P 500 is still in a correction after a rough November.

global.title: AI shares rebound, but November is still deep in the red

status.technical: S&P 500 1.60%, Dow 1.18%, Nasdaq Composite 2.31% on the day; WSJ said the Nasdaq finished its best week since April. Mint noted major indexes remain on track for steep November losses amid concerns about AI spending, regulation and higher interest rates. VIX closed at 23.81.
status.layman: US stocks rose Friday and the Nasdaq had its best week since April, the WSJ said. But Mint says stocks are still headed for steep November losses on worries about AI spending, regulation and interest rates.

consequence.technical: Reuters said the sliding market now faces jobs data and the rate view as its next tests; if hotter inflation lifts expectations of a December Fed hike (Mint), pressure on equities could return. CNBC noted a correction does not always lead to a bear market or recession.
consequence.layman: Reuters says jobs data and interest-rate hopes are the next tests. If a Fed rate rise looks likelier, stocks could wobble again. CNBC says a correction does not always lead to something worse.

impact.technical: The FT said political meddling over Nvidia has rubbed gloss off the dollar and Treasuries and is now hitting equities. Gold rose 3.75% on the day, while Mint said Fed hike risks linger.
impact.layman: The FT says political interference over Nvidia has already hurt confidence in the dollar and US government bonds, and is now reaching stocks. Gold rose 3.75%, Mint said.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after one-day rises above 1 standard deviation, the S&P 500 rose the next day 51% of 192 times (median 0%) and over 5 days 53% of 191 times (median 0.23%, 10th-90th pct -3.28% to 2.84%).
outlook.layman: After big one-day jumps in the past, the S&P 500 rose the next day 51% of 192 times, about a coin flip. That is history, not a prediction.

regions.title: Americas: US rebounds, Brazil's cabinet picks cheer markets

status.technical: S&P 500 1.60%, Dow 1.18%, Nasdaq Composite 2.31%, Russell 2000 1.71%, TSX 1.26%, IPC 1.98%; Bovespa 0.20% (5d 6.48%). Bloomberg reported Brazil assets surged after Lula tapped Trabuco as finance chief.
status.layman: US, Canadian and Mexican stocks all rose. Brazil's market has risen over the week after President Lula chose a banker as finance chief, Bloomberg said.

consequence.technical: If Lula's market-friendly picks hold (Bloomberg said they signal a more pragmatic economic approach), Brazilian assets could stay supported; the US rebound still sits within a month of steep AI-related losses (Mint).
consequence.layman: If Lula keeps choosing market-friendly officials, Brazil's markets may stay calmer. In the US, the bounce follows a month of big losses.

impact.technical: Bloomberg said the week's message from Washington was that the government will intervene to win the AI race with China; US tech holders and index investors are exposed to that policy swing.
impact.layman: Bloomberg said Washington promised to step in to help the US win the AI race with China. People who own US tech stocks or index funds feel that most.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after one-day rises above 1 standard deviation, the Nasdaq Composite rose the next day 53% of 196 times and over 5 days 53% of 195 times (10th-90th pct -4.12% to 3.18%).
outlook.layman: After big one-day gains in the past, the Nasdaq rose the next day 53% of 196 times. That is history, not a forecast.

regions.title: Europe: broad gains as tariff worries ease

status.technical: FTSE 100 0.84%, DAX 0.90%, CAC 40 0.58%, Euro Stoxx 50 1.24%. Yahoo Finance UK reported European stocks rallied as US tariff concerns eased and falling bond yields supported sentiment; Morningstar said Imperial Brands lit up the FTSE.
status.layman: Stock markets across Europe rose. Yahoo Finance UK said worries about US tariffs eased, and lower bond yields helped. London got a lift from Imperial Brands, Morningstar said.

consequence.technical: Economic Times reported eurozone bond yields edged higher on Friday as investors returned to riskier assets and oil rebounded; if yields keep rising, the support from falling yields cited earlier could fade.
consequence.layman: Economic Times says European bond yields ticked up on Friday. If they keep rising, one of the reasons stocks rose could fade.

impact.technical: The WSJ reported inflation fell more than expected in France and Spain in November on declining fuel prices, and the eurozone economy grew less than previously estimated. CNBC reported SAP is reportedly cutting at least 10,000 jobs.
impact.layman: Prices rose more slowly in France and Spain thanks to cheaper fuel, the WSJ said, though the euro area grew less than first thought. SAP is reportedly cutting at least 10,000 jobs, CNBC said.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after one-day rises above 1 standard deviation, the Euro Stoxx 50 rose the next day 50% of 188 times and over 5 days 54% of 186 times (median 0.32%, 10th-90th pct -2.67% to 2.57%).
outlook.layman: After big one-day rises in the past, Europe's Euro Stoxx 50 rose the next day 50% of 188 times, a coin flip. That is history, not a forecast.

regions.title: Asia-Pacific: China support lifts sentiment, AI unwind lingers

status.technical: Investing.com said the Nikkei 225 closed up 2.11%; FT reported Chinese shares soared after Beijing signalled more support, the CSI 300's biggest one-day rise in two years. Latest closes: TAIEX 2.50%, Hang Seng 1.19%, KOSPI 0.29%, Australia's ASX 0.80%. Mint said Nifty 50 was down 1.07%.
status.layman: Japan's Nikkei rose 2.11%, and Chinese shares jumped after Beijing promised more support, the FT said. India's Nifty 50 fell, Mint reported, on profit-taking after a strong month.

consequence.technical: If Beijing follows through on market support (FT, Reuters), Chinese stocks may stay steadier; Mint says KOSPI has fallen 48% from its record high and Bloomberg says foreign funds are on pace for a record Taiwan exodus, so AI-unwind stress remains.
consequence.layman: If China backs up its promise, its stocks may calm. But Korea's index is down 48% from its peak and foreign investors are pulling out of Taiwan, so stress remains.

impact.technical: Bloomberg said the Kospi rout wiped $151 Billion from Korea's pension fund's assets. Bloomberg said Taiwan raised its 2027 growth outlook despite AI worries.
impact.layman: Korea's big pension fund lost a lot as its stock market fell, Bloomberg reported. Taiwan still raised its growth forecast for 2027.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after one-day rises above 1 standard deviation, TAIEX rose the next day 61% of 189 times and over 5 days 61% of 187 times (median 0.61%); Australia's ASX rose 54% of 178 times and the Hang Seng 50% of 175 times.
outlook.layman: After big one-day gains in the past, Taiwan's market rose the next day 61% of 189 times. That is history, not a forecast.

drivers.title: AI trade volatility after Nvidia's CEO drama

status.technical: CNBC said Huang's return sparked only a fleeting AI rally and volatility persisted; Bloomberg called it a wild Thanksgiving week as Washington said it would intervene to win the AI race with China. Nvidia +0.80% (1d), Broadcom +3.82% (1d).
status.layman: CNBC said Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia gave AI stocks only a brief lift. Bloomberg called it a wild week as Washington pledged to help the US win the AI race.

consequence.technical: If concerns about AI spending and regulation persist (Mint), volatility could return; the FT said the Nvidia intervention carries a cost for US stocks.
consequence.layman: If worries about AI spending and new rules last, wild swings could come back. The FT says the Nvidia episode has a cost for US stocks.

impact.technical: Mint reported SanDisk, AMD and Broadcom rebounded; Bloomberg said Anthropic shares climbed above their $83 IPO price after a volatile first week. Evidence is thin on effects outside US tech.
impact.layman: AI-linked shares such as SanDisk, AMD and Broadcom bounced back, Mint said. The notes say little about who else is affected.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after one-day rises above 1 standard deviation, the Nasdaq Composite rose the next day 53% of 196 times (median 0.06%) and over 5 days 53% of 195 times.
outlook.layman: In past cases like this, the Nasdaq rose the next day 53% of 196 times. That is history, not a prediction.

drivers.title: Fed rate-hike risk and Treasury yields

status.technical: Mint reported hotter-than-expected US core inflation raised expectations of a possible December Fed rate hike; Reuters said the Canadian dollar held a weekly gain as investors bet on a December rate hike. The US 10-year yield closed at 4.94, up 1.82%.
status.layman: Mint said hotter US inflation has raised hopes of a Fed interest-rate rise in December. The 10-year US government bond yield rose 1.82% to 4.94.

consequence.technical: If a December hike is delivered, Mint said it could strengthen the dollar; CNBC's Liesman said Nvidia whiplash tests Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's push to read market signals.
consequence.layman: If the Fed does raise rates, Mint says the dollar could get stronger. CNBC says this week's market swings make the Fed's job harder.

impact.technical: Mint said gold pared gains as Fed hike risks linger. Borrowers and bond holders are most exposed to yield moves; the notes give little detail beyond that.
impact.layman: Gold gave back some gains because people worry about a rate rise, Mint said. Anyone with a loan is exposed to rate moves.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after one-day rises above 1 standard deviation, the 10-year yield rose the next day 52% of 184 times (median 0.17%) and over 5 days 52% of 184 times.
outlook.layman: In the past, after big one-day rises the 10-year yield rose the next day 52% of 184 times. That is history, not a forecast.

status.technical: US Dollar Index closed at 104.05, up 0.37%; USD/INR closed at 92.98, up 0.80%. Reuters reported US stock selloffs trigger a new kind of dollar bounce.
status.layman: The US dollar rose again. Reuters says that when US stocks fall, investors now tend to buy dollars.

consequence.technical: If a December Fed hike materialises, Mint said it could strengthen the dollar; the FT said political meddling has rubbed gloss off the dollar, so the pattern may be unstable.
consequence.layman: If the Fed raises rates, the dollar could get stronger. The FT says political interference has hurt the dollar's appeal, so the picture is mixed.

impact.technical: Mint listed rupee weakness among reasons Indian stocks fell; Business Standard said IT and bank heavyweights dragged markets down 1% amid rising crude prices and rupee weakness.
impact.layman: A weaker rupee was one reason Indian stocks fell, according to Mint and Business Standard.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after one-day rises above 1 standard deviation, the US Dollar Index rose the next day 52% of 190 times (median 0.03%) and over 5 days 53% of 189 times.
outlook.layman: After big one-day rises in the past, the dollar rose the next day 52% of 190 times. That is history, not a forecast.

drivers.title: Oil, Iran tensions and OPEC+ talks

status.technical: Brent closed at 90.57, -4.27%; WTI closed at 83.01, -0.80%. WSJ reported the US struck a vessel attempting a blockade run near Iran as diplomatic talks hit a wall; Economic Times said OPEC+ is expected to keep production targets for Q1 2027.
status.layman: Oil fell on Friday. The WSJ said the US struck a ship trying to run its blockade near Iran while talks stalled. OPEC+ is expected to keep its output targets steady, Economic Times said.

consequence.technical: Business Standard said rising crude prices weighed on Indian stocks, while Financial Express said OPEC+ faces crucial talks as Gulf supplies recover; if the Iran standoff escalates, oil-sensitive markets could stay volatile.
consequence.layman: Business Standard linked rising crude to falling Indian stocks. If the Iran standoff gets worse, oil-sensitive markets could stay choppy.

impact.technical: CNBC reported budget airline Norse Atlantic filed for bankruptcy after soaring fuel costs strained its operations; Financial Express said India eyes price relief.
impact.layman: Airline Norse Atlantic went bankrupt after high fuel costs, CNBC said. India hopes for cheaper oil, Financial Express said.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after one-day falls bigger than 1 standard deviation, Brent rose the next day 49% of 172 times (median -0.03%) and over 5 days 53% of 171 times (10th-90th pct -6.18% to 7.17%).
outlook.layman: In the past, after big one-day drops oil rose the next day 49% of 172 times, a coin flip. That is not a forecast.

status.technical: FT reported Chinese shares soared after Beijing signalled more support; Economic Times said copper prices rose after China's cabinet announced support for the stock market. Copper closed at 5.60, up 5.03%.
status.layman: China promised more help for its stock market. Economic Times said copper prices jumped on the news, and the FT said Chinese shares surged.

consequence.technical: If support continues (Reuters), the lift to Chinese equities and copper could persist; Economic Times noted the copper rise follows a significant drop earlier this month.
consequence.layman: If China keeps its promise, shares and copper may hold their gains. Copper had dropped a lot earlier this month, Economic Times said.

impact.technical: Economic Times said China's industrial profits were also reported; evidence on wider effects is thin in the notes.
impact.layman: The notes say little about who else is affected by China's steps.

outlook.layman: After big one-day rises in the past, Hong Kong's Hang Seng rose the next day 50% of 175 times. That is history, not a forecast.
